questions.prompt: What reminded Mrs Slade of the time they went to the island? J
questions.passage:
Mrs Slade sat back on her deck chair and sipped her lemonade up through the ice-cubes. Her friend Mrs Anstis was there too, leaning on the low stone wall that ran around the perimeter of the rooftop garden. She was gazing down on the city, which was bathed in the golden light that sometimes is seen near the end of the day.

"This reminds me of the time we went to the island," said Mrs Slade.

"How? This is nothing like the island."

"The warm evenings, and the light. And it's so peaceful," replied Mrs Slade. "There's no beach here thank goodness. I really didn't want all that sand and salt this year."

"So that's why you chose this place for our holiday!" replied her friend, rattling the ice in her glass.

questions.prompt: Why did Fran take her wisdom teeth home with her? JR
questions.passage:
Fran had her wisdom teeth pulled out by the dentist. She took them home with her and put them in a matchbox on a shelf in her bedroom. She didn't like to think of them being thrown out.

One day, not feeling well, she came home early from work. She lay on her bed, her eyes closed. She hadn't been there very long before her young brother entered the room unaware that Fran was there. Silently she watched him take her matchbox from his pocket and place it carefully on the shelf. Caught red-handed, he had to explain. Her teeth were making him money. He had been letting the kids at school look at her wisdom teeth for a dollar a turn.

questions.prompt: A French Army officer entered a cave in the desert and found himself gazing at an art gallery which was later proved to date back 8 000 years in parts.
questions.passage:
SAHARA

The Sahara Desert, vast, dry, stark and hot, covers much of Northern Africa.

But 8 000 years ago, the Central Sahara was a green, fertile plain. We know this because in 1933 an amazing discovery was made.

The paintings had been put on the dry sandstone walls over a period of thousands of years, and record the history of the land and people of several ages. The earliest pictures show animals that are now extinct and others such as rhino, hippo and giraffe - all of which are now only to be found 1500 kilometres further south. They also show dark skinned hunters with bows and arrows, scenes of their family life, hunting parties and herds of cattle.

Later ones show paler figures in more detail; wearing belts, anklets and rings. There are wedding ceremonies and many domestic scenes. Hunting scenes show sheep, giraffes and elephants. Still later, the warriors are dressed in tunics and they are in chariots.

As the climate changed, the water courses dried up. No longer able to live in numbers in the dry and dying land, the population decreased and very little was added to the cave art gallery.
